description: Generic Kotlin Multiplatform app (Android + iOS, Compose Multiplatform): build-logic convention plugins, core/* modules (design system with Liquid Glass, MVI, Ktor network + auth refresh, mock engine, storage, security, realtime/Socket.IO, analytics, Firebase ports, notifications, navigation, DI), feature/sample, CI policy scripts, detekt, .claude rules/roles/session/memory. Snapshot of KMP_TEMPLATE output with the sentinel identity 'Acme Shop' / com.acme.shop / AcmeShop (see README.md).

source.tool: a KMP generator (not part of this repository); the snapshot is maintained by hand, see README.md section 4

derived_placeholders.__APP_PACKAGE_DASHED__: the package with '-' instead of '.', e.g. com-acme-shop (Gradle version-catalog plugin aliases in gradle/libs.versions.toml)
derived_placeholders.__APP_PACKAGE_PATH__: the package with '/' instead of '.', e.g. com/acme/shop (Kotlin source folders and config/policy-baseline.json keys)
derived_placeholders.__DEV_API_HOST__: host of __DEV_API_URL__ (xcconfig writes URLs as https:/$()/host, so only the host is a literal there)

sentinel_order: replace the longest literal first (full URLs before bare hosts, com.acme.shop before AcmeShop); plain string replacement, no regex

com.acme.shop: every Kotlin file (package/import lines) under androidApp, composeApp, core/*, feature/*, build-logic
com/acme/shop: directory names src/<sourceSet>/kotlin/com/acme/shop/** (56 folders) and build-logic/.../com/acme/shop/buildlogic
https://api.example.com | api.example.co: scripts/ci/tests/test_hardcoded.py (a test literal; any https URL keeps the test valid)
Acme-Server: KDoc comments in core/network (ErrorEnvelopeDto, AuthEndpoints, RemoteTokenRefreshApi), core/data/BaseResponse.kt, core/realtime tests

rename_paths_note: Package-path rename rule: Kotlin source trees are folders, so for EVERY file compute dest = substitute(path relative to project/, rename_paths, longest literal first) and create its parents before writing the substituted content; then verify no sentinel is left in any path or text file. `AcmeShop` is kept in rename_paths for forward compatibility (no file or folder is literally named AcmeShop today). Dev applicationId / iOS dev bundle id = __APP_PACKAGE__ + '.dev' (DEV_APPLICATION_ID_SUFFIX / BUNDLE_ID_SUFFIX), nothing to rename for it.

targeted.why: '/app' is too short to replace globally (Socket.IO protocol tests use '40/app,' packets as fixed test data). SocketIoRealtimeClientTest therefore pins `namespace = TEST_NAMESPACE` ("/app") on its RealtimeConfig instead of relying on the default; a test that depended on the default broke with any other namespace (found with Beta Store, fixed in the snapshot 2026-10-28).
the business time zone default comes from the business answer; UTC is used while it is TBD

not_in_snapshot.__APP_DIR__: the target folder name; no literal inside the files
not_in_snapshot.__SYSTEM_NAME__: no literal; no literal; neutral test data (reference numbers 'REF-1001', a localization test string 'ZED') and the lint cache dir name kmp-app-lint
not_in_snapshot.__SYSTEM_PREFIX__: no literal (task prefixes are not used inside the app)

firebase: androidApp/src/{dev,prod}/google-services.json and iosApp/Firebase/{dev,prod}/GoogleService-Info.plist are PLACEHOLDERS (Firebase stays off until replaced); after substitution their ids are __APP_PACKAGE__.dev / __APP_PACKAGE__. Their project ids are the neutral literals firebase-dev-placeholder / firebase-prod-placeholder (KMP_TEMPLATE emits <last package segment>-dev-placeholder, i.e. shop-dev-placeholder; neutralize it when regenerating the snapshot). Real files must never be committed to the template.
contract: No OpenAPI spec is shipped (docs/api/openapi.json absent, so the contract check is skipped). `./gradlew apiSync` reads ../__SERVER_DIR__/docs/api/openapi.customer.json by default; pass --spec for another file name.
neutral_literals: REF-1001 / REF-Z4JSMB / REF-RM7GX8 reference numbers and help@example.com in test data

verified.results: 553 files, 56 package folders renamed, no sentinel left; policy tests 93 OK; policy_checks all ok; detekt 0 findings; gradle testAndroidHostTest + :androidApp:assembleDevDebug + :composeApp:linkDebugFrameworkIosSimulatorArm64 — see README.md §3

regenerate: not regenerated: the snapshot is maintained by hand, see README.md section 4

edits.find:
ios:
    name: iOS ${{ matrix.scheme }} ${{ matrix.configuration }}
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { scheme: iosApp-Dev, configuration: Debug-Dev }
          - { scheme: iosApp-Dev, configuration: Release-Dev }
          - { scheme: iosApp-Prod, configuration: Debug-Prod }
          - { scheme: iosApp-Prod, configuration: Release-Prod }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 21
      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4
      - uses: maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode@v1
        with:
          xcode-version: latest-stable
      # The Xcode "Compile Kotlin Framework" phase runs Gradle; warnings are errors (see the project build settings).
      - name: Build for the iOS simulator
        run: >-
          xcodebuild
          -project iosApp/iosApp.xcodeproj
          -scheme ${{ matrix.scheme }}
          -configuration ${{ matrix.configuration }}
          -sdk iphonesimulator
          -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator'
          CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO
          build
      - name: Kotlin/Native unit tests
        if: matrix.configuration == 'Debug-Dev'
        run: ./gradlew iosSimulatorArm64Test --stacktrace
      - name: SwiftLint
        if: matrix.configuration == 'Debug-Dev'
        run: |
          brew install swiftlint
          swiftlint lint --strict --config config/swiftlint.yml
and every iOS configuration (xcodebuild + Kotlin/Native tests + SwiftLint).

android:
    name: Android ${{ matrix.flavor }} ${{ matrix.buildType }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { flavor: dev, buildType: debug, task: DevDebug }
          - { flavor: dev, buildType: release, task: DevRelease }
          - { flavor: prod, buildType: debug, task: ProdDebug }
          - { flavor: prod, buildType: release, task: ProdRelease }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 21
      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4
      - name: Assemble
        run: ./gradlew :androidApp:assemble${{ matrix.task }} --stacktrace
      - name: Android Lint (warnings are errors)
        run: ./gradlew :androidApp:lint${{ matrix.task }} --stacktrace
      - name: Print Android Lint findings
        if: failure()
        run: cat androidApp/build/reports/lint-results-*.txt 2>/dev/null | head -300 || true
      # commonTest of every module, run on the JVM.
      - name: Unit tests
        if: matrix.task == 'DevDebug'
        run: ./gradlew testAndroidHostTest --stacktrace
      - name: Performance budget (R8 mapping and APK size)
        if: matrix.buildType == 'release'
        run: python3 scripts/ci/policy_checks.py budget --flavor ${{ matrix.flavor }}
      - name: Upload reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: android-reports-${{ matrix.task }}
          path: |
            androidApp/build/reports
            **/build/reports/tests
          if-no-files-found: ignore

every Android variant (assemble + lint +
# unit tests + R8/APK-size budget) and every iOS configuration

prune_note: Platform choice. A group is applied when the app did NOT choose that platform (an Android-only app drops `ios`, an iOS-only app drops `android`): its `skip` globs are not copied, its `edits` (exact find -> replace_with on the generated files; a text that is missing is an error) remove the Gradle targets, the settings entry and the CI job, and its `post_generate` commands are not listed. Android-only: no iosApp folder, no iOS target in any build file, no iOS CI job. iOS-only: no androidApp folder, module, CI job or Android policy variants; the shared modules keep their Android library target because the convention plugins apply it to every module, so an iOS-only app still needs the Android SDK to configure Gradle (not built or proven).
